intended_object: The ordered simplex {t ∈ ℝⁿ : 1 ≥ t₀ ≥ t₁ ≥ … ≥ t_{n−1} ≥ 0}, i.e. the decreasing chain of parameters in [0,1] that appears in the BKAR forest formula. The docstring calls it "the ordered finite simplex in `Fin n` coordinates", and the library uses it as the target of the ordered coordinate equivalence.
explanation:
The definition unfolds `OrderedSimplexParams 1 (List.ofFn ts)` recursively: `OrderedSimplexParams top (t :: ts)` means `0 ≤ t ∧ t ≤ top ∧ OrderedSimplexParams t ts`. So the predicate says exactly 0 ≤ t_{n−1} ≤ … ≤ t₀ ≤ 1. Each coordinate is ≥ 0 and ≤ 1, so the extra cube condition `∀ i, 0 ≤ ts i ∧ ts i ≤ 1` adds nothing. The docstring says the cube bounds are included on purpose, and they are harmless.

Degenerate case: for n = 0 the set is the single point in ℝ⁰, which is the expected value.

The result is the standard ordered simplex {1 ≥ t₁ ≥ … ≥ t_n ≥ 0}. Mathlib has no definition of this set. `stdSimplex` is the barycentric simplex, a different object. Defining it over ℝ with `Fin n` coordinates fits its role as Lebesgue-measurable integration domains in the BKAR formula, so it is not too narrow.
